pr_title: Add support for a second Ethernet controller in the MCUX driver
pr_body:
Closes #23284.

This PR allows using the second Ethernet controller of the i.MXRT1060 family.
pr_comments:
It is mostly ready, but I still need to do more testing before removing WIP status. Please review and comment.

I also plan to make the PHY address defined in the device tree, but I'm still undecided if I do it in a separated PR or not.

issue_context.title: driver: ethernet: Add support for a second Ethernet controller in the MCUX driver
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
MCUs from the i.MX RT1060 family are equipped with 2 Ethernet controllers but the MCUX driver does support only the first one (ENET base register is hard-coded).

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Modify the driver so that it can support multiple controllers.

**Additional context**
I have a proof of concept barely working, that I can share in order to discuss how to properly implement the changes (I've modified DTS and the driver itself).
comments:
>  I can share in order to discuss how to properly implement the changes

That is a good idea so please share your changes.

@jukkar I'm cleaning up my proof of concept so that it can be merged. It is not finished yet but you can already have a look here: [eth_mcux_enet2](https://github.com/riedonetworks/zephyr/tree/eth_mcux_enet2)
@armandciejak good to see you are making this driver multi-instance!
@agansari I'm changing quite a few things, shall I already open a pull request even if I'm not finished with the changes? I would like to get comments ASAP.
@armandciejak sure, think you can tag it as WIP or DNM until it's close to a merge state

> @armandciejak sure, think you can tag it as WIP or DNM until it's close to a merge state

One option is also to create the PR as a draft.

review_comments: The device tree bindings have a "max-speed" property which tells the maximum speed of the interface (or what the user wants it to be). Therefore this shouldn't be hard-coded but derived from the DT. Because this is an optional binding, we will have to fallback to this number if "max-speed" is unspecified in the DT.
@bwasim It sounds good to me but I think it is out of scope for this PR since I didn't change that part.
I understand the concept of keeping changes limited but this is something that should be done eventually..
There is no value in making the phy_addr a 32-bit variable as the number of PHYs connected to a MAC instance can never be more than 31. An 8-bit variable (u8_t) will do here.
@bwasim OK but phy_addr is a 32-bit unsigned integer parameter in all functions (e.g. ENET_StartSMIWrite).

This "generate_random_mac" address function is not limited to the NXP Ethernet driver and can be used by any driver. Therefore I feel that this should be made global and placed in some generic file from where all drivers can access it. Will help reduce redundancy.. 

Otherwise we will see all drivers keep a copy of a function which generates a random MAC address. Is there some file which processes the Ethernet L2 header ? That will be the best place for this to go in.
